title: Heliograph — Sundial Workbench
description: Design a working sundial for any latitude, run the shadow through a year, and print the template.
concept: A 3D workbench for the oldest instrument there is. Pick one of four dial types — horizontal, vertical, equatorial or analemmatic — drop it at any latitude and longitude, and watch a real cast shadow sweep the plate as you scrub the clock and the calendar. Hour lines come from the actual solar geometry rather than a drawing, the nodus traces declination curves and a full analemma, and the whole dial exports as a true-scale SVG with a gnomon cutting template you can print and build.
features: Four dial types with correct hour-line geometry — horizontal (tan θ = sin φ tan H), vertical, equatorial and the gnomon-less analemmatic ellipse
Site setup: latitude, longitude and UTC offset sliders plus twelve city presets, both hemispheres handled
Time machine: clock and date scrubbers with animate-the-day and animate-the-year playback
Markings you can switch on — declination curves for the solstices and equinox, the year-long analemma trace at a fixed clock hour, the day's sun path, nodus height
Live readouts: altitude, azimuth, apparent solar time, equation of time, sunrise/sunset, shadow ratio, lit face
Export a true-scale SVG dial template with a gnomon cutting triangle, a PNG of the 3D view, and a share link that carries the whole dial in the URL
localStorage persistence and orbit/pinch camera control
tech: NOAA solar position + equation of time series

interaction.mouse: Drag to orbit the dial, scroll to zoom
interaction.click: Switch dial type, pick a city, toggle markings, export PNG/SVG or copy a share link
interaction.touch: Drag to orbit, pinch to zoom, pull the bottom sheet up for controls
interaction.keyboard: Space plays the day · ←/→ shift time · ↑/↓ shift date · 1–4 pick a dial · E saves a PNG
